legal_aid.name: Alameda County Public Defender — Clean Slate Program
legal_aid.what: Record relief: felony-to-misdemeanor reductions, Prop 47/64 relief, early probation termination, dismissals, certificates of rehabilitation, human-trafficking vacatur, PC 290 relief. Walk-in clinics at 545 4th St, Oakland, start 9:00 a.m. (intakes stop 11:00 a.m.); 2026 dates posted: 10/22, 11/5, 11/19, 12/3. Most dismissals require no pending case and not on probation/parole.

programs.name: Pretrial Release Program (Superior Court Pretrial Services)
programs.summary: Run by the Superior Court. Alternatives to cash bail and pretrial detention for people with pending Alameda County criminal cases; services based on court orders, risk assessment and needs, aiming to reduce missed court dates and rearrests. Court warns: Pretrial Services never asks defendants or families for money (scammers impersonate them demanding GPS/ankle-monitor payments).
programs.todo: Email listed: PretrialServices@alameda.courts.ca.gov; office address not listed

programs.name: Drug Court
programs.summary: For people with drug/alcohol and co-occurring conditions. Misdemeanor court (Wiley W. Manuel, D-114, 1st & 3rd Mondays) and felony court (Wiley W. Manuel, D-106, Mondays weeks 1–4).

programs.name: Veterans Treatment Court
programs.summary: Wiley W. Manuel Courthouse, D-106, 2nd & 4th Fridays.

programs.name: Reentry Court
programs.summary: Wiley W. Manuel Courthouse, D-106, 1st & 3rd Tuesdays.

programs.name: Early Intervention Court (EIC)
programs.summary: Diversion for low-level (PC 1170(h)) felonies, case-managed by Leaders in Community Alternatives; about one year; completion can lead to dismissal and PC 851.91 relief. Referral by DA agreement; typically excludes gun, DV and PC 290 offenses.

programs.name: Behavioral Health Court (BHC)
programs.summary: For people with severe mental illness; case-managed by Alameda County Behavioral Health; about one year. DA offer required; must be Alameda County Medi-Cal eligible with no private insurance; DV and most gun cases excluded.

programs.name: 1370.01 Calendar and DSH Diversion
programs.summary: Treatment court for people found incompetent to stand trial: misdemeanor IST cases and selected felony IST cases (DSH Diversion); treatment in community settings.

jails.name: Santa Rita Jail
jails.phone_note: Lobby line (per visiting page). In-person visits by appointment only, booked online up to 3 days ahead; video visits via ViaPath (gettingout.com / alamedaca.gtlvisitme.com, support 1-855-208-7349). Professional visits 9 a.m.–4 p.m. and 6–8:30 p.m.
jails.todo: Only county jail currently (Glenn E. Dyer in Oakland closed 2019 per news reports, not on sheriff's directory). 'both' is based on sheriff population statistics postings listing male and female counts (seen via search index; PDF blocked). Official money-deposit/commissary page not found. court_ids: nearest criminal courthouse, not confirmed — people are transported to whichever courthouse holds their case.

bail.note: CA Department of Insurance 'Check a License' to verify a bail agent's license. The Alameda County Sheriff's homepage warns of scams claiming a Santa Rita inmate can be released early by paying for an ankle monitor — ACSO never calls/texts/emails demanding payment; the court says Pretrial Services never asks for money. Where/how to pay cash bail at Santa Rita was not found on an official page.
